title: High-Risk Endometrial Cancer: Adjuvant RT, Chemotherapy & Immunotherapy
subject: ss-gynaecological-oncology
refs: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology 11e Ch 84
NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Uterine Neoplasms (2024)

steps.say: Landmark international clinical trials have redefined adjuvant therapy for women with high risk endometrial cancer. Combined modality treatment significantly improves overall and failure free survival in Stage III cohorts.
steps.tx: The randomized phase **3** **PORTEC-3 trial** demonstrated that adjuvant **chemoradiotherapy** (external pelvic radiation concurrent with **2** cycles of cisplatin followed by **4** cycles of adjuvant **carboplatin paclitaxel**) yielded significant **survival benefit in high-risk** Stage III disease, increasing **5**-year overall survival from **69** percent to **76** percent.

vis.alt: High-risk endometrial cancer adjuvant management pathways

steps.say: The choice between systemic chemotherapy alone and combined chemoradiation was directly evaluated in a major cooperative group trial. Adding radiation dramatically reduces pelvic and para aortic nodal recurrences.
steps.tx: In protocol **GOG-258**, evaluating **chemotherapy vs chemoradiation** (**6** cycles of carboplatin-paclitaxel versus chemoradiotherapy) in advanced Stage **3** and **4** disease, chemoradiotherapy produced significant **pelvic recurrence reduction** (**11** percent vs **20** percent) and lowered para-aortic relapses, despite equivalence in overall progression-free survival.

left.title: Adjuvant Chemoradiotherapy (GOG-258 / PORTEC-3)
points: External beam radiation + concurrent cisplatin + carboplatin/paclitaxel
Significantly reduces pelvic locoregional recurrences (11% vs 20%)

right.title: Chemotherapy Alone (6 Cycles Carboplatin/Paclitaxel)
points: Higher incidence of pelvic and vaginal vault failure
Avoids long-term pelvic radiation enteritis and bowel toxicity

steps.say: For intermediate risk disease without adverse histological features, local vaginal treatment achieves equivalent disease control with minimal bowel toxicity. Brachytherapy replaces external pelvic beams in this setting.
steps.tx: In **high-intermediate risk** early endometrial carcinoma, the landmark **PORTEC-2 trial** established that **vaginal brachytherapy (VBT)** alone achieves vaginal vault local control equivalent to external beam pelvic radiotherapy (vault relapse <**2** percent) while producing marked **GI toxicity reduction**, avoiding chronic radiation proctitis and enteritis.

rows: Cervical stroma invasion, positive pelvic nodes
Stage III, serous, or clear cell carcinoma

steps.say: Immune checkpoint inhibition combined with platinum doublet chemotherapy has transformed first line systemic therapy for mismatch repair deficient neoplasms. The addition of dostarlimab produces unprecedented progression free survival improvements.
steps.tx: In the phase **3** **RUBY trial**, adding the anti-PD-**1** monoclonal antibody **dostarlimab** to carboplatin and paclitaxel in advanced or recurrent **dMMR/MSI-H** endometrial carcinoma resulted in a dramatic **PFS HR 0.28** (progression-free survival hazard ratio **0.28**), with **72** percent of dMMR patients remaining progression-free at two years.

nodes.label: Identify advanced stage III/IV or first recurrent endometrial carcinoma
Confirm dMMR/MSI-H status on universal tumor testing
Administer dostarlimab (500 mg Q3W) with carboplatin and paclitaxel
Continue dostarlimab maintenance (1000 mg Q6W) for up to 3 years

steps.say: A parallel cooperative trial confirmed that pembrolizumab yields similar breakthrough benefits when combined with standard chemotherapy. Therapeutic advantage is seen in both mismatch repair deficient and proficient populations.
steps.tx: The randomized phase III trial **NRG-GY018** demonstrated that adding **pembrolizumab** to carboplatin and paclitaxel in advanced endometrial cancer yielded an outstanding **dMMR HR 0.30** (**70** percent risk reduction) and a statistically significant **pMMR HR 0.54** (hazard ratio **0.54**, **18**-month PFS improvement), establishing front-line checkpoint inhibition across subtypes.

left.title: dMMR Cohort (NRG-GY018)
points: Durable immune checkpoint clonal neoantigen response

right.title: pMMR Cohort (NRG-GY018)
points: Median PFS increased from 8.7 to 13.1 months
Statistically significant clinical benefit in proficient tumors

steps.say: For patients with mismatch repair proficient disease progressing after prior chemotherapy, multi kinase inhibition combined with immunotherapy provides a standard second line regimen. Lenvatinib synergizes with pembrolizumab.
steps.tx: In the phase III trial **KEYNOTE-775**, the combination of **pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib** demonstrated significant overall survival and progression-free survival superiority over physician-choice chemotherapy for **pMMR recurrence** in patients progressing after prior platinum therapy, establishing an approved **TKI immunotherapy** standard regimen.

steps.say: Uterine serous carcinoma frequently overexpresses the human epidermal growth factor receptor two oncoprotein. Incorporating targeted anti HER2 therapy prolongs progression free survival.
steps.tx: In aggressive **uterine serous carcinoma**, approximately **30** percent of tumors exhibit **HER2 overexpression** (IHC **3**+ or FISH amplified). Adding the monoclonal antibody **trastuzumab** to carboplatin and paclitaxel significantly extended median **PFS 12.6 months** versus **8.0** months for chemotherapy alone in advanced or recurrent disease.

nodes.label: Diagnose uterine serous carcinoma on surgical pathology
Perform reflex HER2 immunohistochemistry (IHC) and FISH
Confirm HER2 3+ or FISH amplified positivity (30% prevalence)

steps.say: Indolent low grade recurrent endometrioid carcinomas enriched with estrogen and progesterone receptors respond favorably to hormonal manipulation. Aromatase inhibitors and progestins provide durable disease stabilization.
steps.tx: In **low-grade ER/PR positive** recurrent endometrioid carcinoma without life-threatening visceral crisis, systemic **hormonal therapy** utilizing alternating **megestrol/tamoxifen** or aromatase inhibitors such as **letrozole** (2.5 mg daily) achieves objective response rates of **25** to **30** percent with prolonged disease stabilization and minimal toxicity.
